newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to seek international jail swaps.
newsitem.headline: Australia to seek international jail swaps.

text.p: Australia's federal and state governments agreed on Friday to seek prisoner swaps with other countries, including Thailand.
Under the scheme, Australians in prison overseas would return to Australian jails, which would send foreign prisoners back to their home countries to complete their sentences.

"There are a number of countries that are interested in entering into bilateral arrangements with us, including Thailand where there are a number of Australian prisoners," Attorney-General Daryl Williams told Australian Broadcasting Corp Radio.
"We then have to negotiate either on a multilateral basis or a bilateral basis with other countries," said Williams, the country's senior legal officer.
Each prisoner would also have to agree to the transfer, a spokesman for Williams said.

At a meeting in Canberra on Friday federal and state ministers agreed to draft legislation to create the system. Williams' spokesman said the states would introduce legislation into their respective parliaments within the next year while federal legislation would be ready by the end of 1996.
The government says 148 Australians were imprisoned abroad at the end of June, about 21 of them in Thailand.
No number was available for the number of foreign nationals in Australian prisons.
